pairs.subject: generative-provider-routing
pairs.evidence: lib/imaging/router.ts:93 The dev generate plan still puts agy first, ahead of Google, which won the measured cost-per-usable grid. agy has no price and no usable-output measurement (router.ts:87 says only 'verified live'), so every dev generate where agy is present routes to an unmeasured vendor. The standard says a new vendor goes in behind the incumbent until a comparison says otherwise.

techniques.evidence: lib/imaging/router.ts:93 agy sits at the head of dev generate without a usable-output comparison, against the rule that a new vendor enters behind the incumbent. The chokepoint and the steer rules themselves are realized (orderFor: avoid removes, and an emptied chain throws no-alternative).

lib/imaging/router.ts:87 agy took the plan's top position on 'verified live', not on cost per usable output. The google/leonardo order is measured (router.ts:81 '$0.052 per usable'), and the pre-call gate is realized (router.ts:312 reserve before any vendor).
lib/imaging/router.ts:405 The trail of eliminations is attached to the served result as provenance.reroutedFrom. Each skip kind is pushed at the moment of decision (e.g. router.ts:370 no-key).

lib/imaging/errors.ts:112 Only refused, rate-limited and no-key re-route, so a vendor timeout or failure throws instead of hopping, which the standard lists as reroutable. There is also no kind for a protected-material block or an account-level stop, so those named reasons cannot throw separately. The core refusal hop is realized.
lib/imaging/pricing.ts:83 Every price row requires a checked date next to its source. Unpriced rows stay undefined with a reason instead of an invented figure.

lib/imaging/types.ts:75 GenerateRequest (lines 75-88) carries aspect, count, references, seed and quality but no size or stage. The gateway therefore cannot ask for a draft rung versus a final rung, and resolution stays a per-vendor env setting.

lib/imaging/handlers.ts:120 GET /api/imaging/budget returns the ceiling, spent and remaining amounts but drops floorUsd and underFloor, although budgetStats computes both. unreachedPlanTops (router.ts:181) has no production caller, only a probe spec. The floor and the uncalled plan top are computed and never reported to a human.
lib/imaging/router.ts:106 recognize leads with the local ollama eye. I did not judge whether that order rests on a bake-off.

pairs.registryProposal: refusal-reroute-hop lists vendor-side failure and timeout as reroutable. errors.ts:85-110 gives a weighed counter-argument: a 5xx or timeout on a billable work request is presumed billed, so a hop bills twice for a request nobody declined. The technique should say when presumed-billed failures should stay unrouted.

pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: lib/articles/types.ts:535 awaiting-approval can leave only by approved, rejected or drafting: there is no expiry edge. grep for expir/overdue/deadline in lib/articles and the decision kernel finds no reaper, so a run at the gate waits forever with no recorded 'expired unanswered' outcome and no overdue marker. The standard says a pending decision must not be immortal.

techniques.evidence: lib/articles/humanActs.ts:35 Approve is a guarded transition allowed only from awaiting-approval (reject likewise at humanActs.ts:47). landing.ts:30 refuses to land a run with no recorded approval.
lib/articles/types.ts:535 There is no timeout edge out of the gate, so expiry never resolves to deny-or-hold as a recorded outcome.

lib/articles/humanActs.ts:36 The run-side approval holds only {at, patches}. The actor and revision live in the Board decision log (packages/kernel/src/decision), outside this context, and I did not judge them.

pairs.evidence: packages/domain/src/run.machine.ts:29 awaiting_gate can go only to ratified, blocked or running: the domain machine has no expiry or overdue state, and no reaper exists in the decision kernel (grep expir/overdue/deadline). packages/domain/src/job.machine.ts:28 Nothing resumes a crashed job automatically. lane.ts:56 holds a paid lane until an operator has looked, so an unknown outcome defaults to stop rather than proceed.
